topic: Dimensional Portals: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices
target_audience: University students (Linear Algebra) and STEM enthusiasts

outline.topic: Dimensional Portals: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices
outline.target_audience: University students (Linear Algebra) and STEM enthusiasts

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Basis of Motion
sections.content: Briefly recap how square matrices (2x2) transform 2D space. Introduce the concept of basis vectors (i-hat and j-hat) and how their landing positions after transformation determine where all other vectors go.
sections.example: Visualizing a 2D grid warping, stretching, and rotating, while i-hat [1,0] and j-hat [0,1] act as the 'DNA' of the transformation.

sections.title: Tall Matrices: Moving Up (2D to 3D)
sections.content: Introduce the 3x2 matrix. Explain that we take 2 input coordinates and map them to 3 output coordinates. Geometrically, this means we are taking a 2D plane and embedding it into 3D space. The two columns of the matrix represent two 3D vectors that span a plane.
sections.example: Imagine a 2D flat 'Paper Mario' character being lifted and placed diagonally into a 3D room. The matrix columns are the 3D coordinates where the character's horizontal and vertical axes land.

sections.title: The 'Span' Perspective
sections.content: Analyze why a 3x2 matrix can't fill the entire 3D space. The output is constrained to a 2D subspace (a slice) within the 3D world. This introduces the concept of 'Column Space' visually.
sections.example: A flashlight shining on a wall: even though the room is 3D, the shadow cast by a 2D shape is still just a flat surface floating in that 3D space.

sections.title: Wide Matrices: Stepping Down (3D to 2D)
sections.content: Introduce the 2x3 matrix. Here, we take 3 input coordinates and map them to 2 output coordinates. This represents a projection or a 'squashing' of 3D space onto a 2D plane. Information is lost (Dimensionality Reduction).
sections.example: A 3D bird flying in a room. A 2x3 matrix acts like a camera lens, projecting the bird's 3D position onto a flat 2D photograph.

sections.title: The Null Space: The Lost Dimension
sections.content: Explain that when moving from 3D to 2D, some directions in 3D must be collapsed to zero. Introduce the Null Space as the line or area that 'disappears' during the transformation.
sections.example: An architect looking directly down at a skyscraper from a helicopter. The height (Z-axis) vanishes into a single point on the 2D blueprint.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Connection
sections.content: Summarize the rule: MxN matrix maps from N-dimensions to M-dimensions. Connect this to modern technology like Neural Networks (changing layer sizes) or Data Compression.
sections.example: Graphic rendering engines converting complex 3D models into 2D pixels on your phone screen using non-square projection matrices.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Basis of Motion
lecture_lines: Square matrices transform input vectors within the same space.
Basis vectors track where every point lands.
These unit vectors are the DNA of transformations.
animations: Show 2D grid #333333 with 2x2 matrix text A = [[a,b],[c,d]] #FFFFFF. Matrix appears with FadeIn.
Create i-hat [1,0] vector #FF0000 and j-hat [0,1] vector #00FF00. Add labels near heads.
Apply matrix transformation to grid and vectors. Grid warps, vectors move to [a,c] and [b,d].

storyboard.title: Tall Matrices: Moving Up (2D to 3D)
lecture_lines: Tall matrices map 2D inputs to 3D outputs.
Two input coordinates become three output coordinates.
This embeds a 2D plane into 3D space.
The matrix columns define where the grid lands.
Our flat world now lives in a larger room.
animations: Show 3x2 matrix template #FFFFFF. 3D coordinate system (X #FF0000, Y #00FF00, Z #0000FF) fades in.
A 2D plane #333333 appears on XY plane. Matrix shifts perspective to 3D.
Draw column vectors v1 #FFFF00 and v2 #00FFFF using Arrows starting at origin.
Create a translucent plane #555555 that is the span of v1 and v2.
Transform a 2D square #FFFFFF from the XY plane to lie flat on the tilted 3D plane.

storyboard.title: The 'Span' Perspective
lecture_lines: A 3x2 matrix cannot fill the entire 3D volume.
The output is trapped on a 2D slice.
This slice is the matrix's column space.
animations: Maintain 3D view with tilted plane #555555. Highlight it with a flashing SurroundingRectangle #FFFF00.
Show a 2D circular shadow #333333 being cast by a 3D sphere onto the tilted plane.
Label the tilted plane 'Column Space' #FFFF00. Fade out the rest of 3D space.

storyboard.title: Wide Matrices: Stepping Down (3D to 2D)
lecture_lines: Wide matrices squash 3D inputs into 2D outputs.
Three input coordinates are projected onto two.
Information is lost as the world flattens.
Think of a 3D bird's shadow on paper.
This is dimensionality reduction in action.
animations: Show 3D grid cube #333333 and 2x3 matrix #FFFFFF. Use smooth transition to center view.
Animate cube squashing along Z-axis into a flat 2D rectangle #555555 on XY plane.
Show 3D vector #FF00FF and its 2D projection (shadow) #FFFFFF on the plane.
Color-code the 3 columns of the 2x3 matrix to match the 3 axes (X #FF0000, Y #00FF00, Z #0000FF).
Fade out the Z-axis #0000FF as the 2D plane becomes the sole focus.

storyboard.title: The Null Space: The Lost Dimension
lecture_lines: Some 3D directions collapse to zero during projection.
The null space contains all vectors that disappear.
A whole line or plane might vanish entirely.
It is the hidden dimension of the transformation.
Where movement is swallowed by the origin.
animations: In 3D, draw a line #FFFF00 representing the Null Space passing through the origin.
Apply the 2x3 transformation: the entire line #FFFF00 collapses into a single dot at the origin.
Show several vectors #00FFFF on that line all moving to (0,0) simultaneously.
Label the origin 'Zero Vector' #FFFFFF and the line 'Null Space' #FFFF00.
Highlight the lost Z-dimension #0000FF as it disappears during the transform.

storyboard.title: Summary & Real-World Connection
lecture_lines: Matrix dimensions dictate the jump between spaces.
From neural networks to computer graphics, this is key.
Non-square matrices are our portals between dimensions.
animations: Display text 'N-dimensions' #00FF00, an arrow #FFFFFF, and 'M-dimensions' #FF00FF.
Show a schematic of a neural network layer with 3 input nodes and 2 output nodes.
A 3D mesh model #00FFFF morphs into a 2D pixel grid #FFFFFF on a screen.
